title: Monotonicity of program bases
statement: Let $n,m,w$ be nonnegative integers, let $\kappa$ be a type of instruction kinds, let $F$ assign an output list of Booleans to each kind and input list, and let $\mathrm{prog}$ be a finite list of instructions with kinds in $\kappa$. For each kind, let its width be the total number of gates in the associated gadgets. The base offset $n+2$ plus the sum of the widths of the first $i$ instructions is nondecreasing in $i$: if $i\le i'$, then the base at $i$ is at most the base at $i'$.
hypotheses_covered: $\kappa$ is a type of instruction kinds
$F$ maps a kind and Boolean list to a Boolean list
$\mathrm{prog}$ is a finite list of instructions with kinds in $\kappa$
